answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow, preventing cheap multiplication. When k coordinated identities equivocate, their aggregate penalties scale quadratically, O(k^2); detection additionally applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss, with asymmetric depreciation accelerating impairment. Splitting stake across velvet, timber, or terrace accounts therefore cannot dilute risk: correlated evidence links the identities and makes coordinated control economically ruinous.
